name: b-event-trail
prompt: Edit this dashboard mockup with exactly one text correction. In the top-right dropdown labelled "Scenarios", replace the value "Pump inspection" with "Lost reply". Preserve every other text, layout, color, position, icon, dimension and styling exactly. The "Pump inspection" label inside the SERVER receipt stays unchanged.
initialPrompt:
Create a polished high-fidelity desktop web dashboard mockup for the existing "Idempotent requests lab". Landscape 1536x1024. This is a static DESIGN PROPOSAL, not evidence of a running application. Use the supplied screenshot ONLY as a reference for navy ink, cobalt actions, flat white/cool-gray surfaces, and readable Atkinson Hyperlegible-style sans typography. Completely replace its page composition and excessive copy. Do not carry over its hero, paragraphs, explanatory footer, large duplicated headings or split-panel card arrangement. Preserve the functional premise: a fictional maintenance request was actually saved by the server, but its reply was lost; the user's next action is retrying the SAME request, which must not create another job. Display precisely the current lost-reply stage, BEFORE retry: one send, one saved request, no client confirmation. Short English labels only, no lorem ipsum, no fake charts, no statistics unrelated to this experiment, no avatars, no marketing, no photorealistic objects, no decorative illustrations, no 3D, no gradients. Deliberate typography, generous but useful spacing, crisp restrained line icons, accessible dark text, compact calm chrome, one blue primary action. Make an implementable premium product UI, full app viewport with no device frame. Show a clear separate "Technical controls" tab. All status colors have text labels. Do not render any design explanation or annotations inside the app.
COMPOSITION B — EVENT TRAIL. A compact header with "Idempotent requests lab" left, "Guided demo" selected and "Technical controls" right. The workspace starts near the top with "02 / 06" above a modest "Lost reply" heading, plus a compact "Scenarios" dropdown to its right. Below, use a deliberately asymmetric 65/35 split with NO enclosing giant card: on the left a short vertical event timeline of exactly three aligned rows. First row small completed green dot on a thin vertical line, "Request sent", secondary label "1 attempt". Second row violet interruption marker, "Reply lost", secondary label "No confirmation". Third row has an open current-step circle and "Try again", with the one cobalt button "Retry same request" directly underneath. Rows have compact vertical rhythm, not chat bubbles. On the right aligned with the middle event, a single small server receipt panel: label "SERVER", one large readable numeral "1", text "saved request", and tiny green-check row "Pump inspection". This panel is evidence, never another action. Below the timeline and receipt a short takeaway "No reply does not mean no save." and collapsed text control "Show explanation". Bottom compact progress six dots and "2 of 6 scenarios". Flat cool white surfaces, navy typography, cobalt button, violet unknown state, green server fact. The left timeline teaches cause and effect through three tiny statements; the right receipt remains the single fact. Keep under 65 visible words. Distinct from presentation mode: left-aligned, sequential, practical and slightly denser but still very sparse.
